faq.a1: It reads a ticket's subject and message and predicts three things: the type (incident, request, problem or change), the area that should handle it (out of 10) and the priority (low, medium or high). Each prediction comes with its confidence level.
faq.a2: If the area confidence falls below the threshold, the ticket isn't sent automatically: it goes to the review queue in the panel and someone on the team picks the area. The panel records who assigned it and when.
faq.a3: It depends on the threshold. Measured on tickets the model never saw, a threshold of 0.50 sends about one in five tickets automatically, and within that group it gets about 85 out of 100 right. The rest go through your team. The threshold board on the home page shows other points.
faq.a4: The model was trained on English tickets. You can write in another language, but confidence will drop and the ticket will most likely go to human review. The interface itself is available in six languages.
faq.a5: They're the ticket terms that pushed the model hardest toward the chosen area. They come from the model itself: each term's weight in the ticket multiplied by its coefficient for that area. It's not text made up to justify the decision.
faq.a6: Not automatically. Assignments are saved, but the model only changes when someone retrains it. That way no single decision changes its behavior without anyone reviewing it.
faq.a7: With the REST API. POST /tickets classifies, saves and routes a ticket; POST /predict only classifies it, without saving anything. The interactive docs are at /docs.
faq.a8: Only admin accounts, from Threshold and areas in the panel. It can be set between 0.30 and 0.90 and applies to new tickets.

privacy.l1: **Tickets:** the subject, the message and the classification result of every ticket you send through the form or the API.
privacy.l2: **Contact messages:** your name, your email and the message, only so we can reply to you.
privacy.l3: **Team accounts:** name, email, role and the password, protected with a key derivation algorithm (never in plain text).
privacy.lede: What data SmartTicket stores, why, and who it shares it with. No fine print.
privacy.p2: We use three cookies, all of them necessary: a session cookie for staff who sign in to the panel, a security cookie that protects forms against forged submissions, and one that remembers your language. We don't use advertising or analytics cookies.
privacy.p3: No one. We don't sell or hand over data. Classification happens on our own server; no ticket is sent to third-party services.
privacy.p4: This instance is a public demo. Don't enter personal data, passwords or sensitive information in test tickets.
privacy.p5: You can ask us to delete a ticket or message you sent. Write to us from the contact page with the ticket code (for example, ST-20412) and we'll delete it.
privacy.title: Privacy notice

terms.lede: The rules for using this site and its API.
terms.p1: SmartTicket classifies support tickets with a machine learning model. Predictions can be wrong; that's why uncertain tickets go to human review. Don't make critical decisions based on a prediction alone.
terms.p2: Don't send illegal content, other people's data without their permission, or automated traffic meant to overload the service. The API has usage limits per IP address; if you exceed them, requests are rejected for a few minutes.
terms.p3: The tickets you send are stored so the team can review them. Since this is a demo, content may be deleted at any time without notice.
terms.p4: SmartTicket's code is open source and distributed under the MIT license. The model was trained on a public dataset licensed under CC BY-NC 4.0, so commercial use of the trained model may be restricted.
terms.p5: The service is provided as is, with no guarantee of availability or accuracy. We may change these terms; the date below shows the current version.
terms.title: Terms of use
